candidates.tagline: Built the most advanced Silverado ever. The screen is 16 inches. The icons are very, very small.
candidates.story: Engadget's first drive of the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado (November 5, 2026) — marketed by GM as the 'most powerful and advanced Silverado ever' with a 16.3-inch main touchscreen — found the control icons so tiny that reviewers couldn't hit the right one while driving; separately, the Super Cruise autonomous system tried to change lanes into a passing motorcycle, requiring the reviewer to grab the wheel.
candidates.why_funny: GM filled America's most macho truck with the biggest screens in the class, then made the icons so small nobody can tap them, and the AI safety feature's first highway trick was to nearly sideswipe a biker.
candidates.alt: 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup truck photographed in green during Engadget's first drive review — GM's self-described most powerful and advanced Silverado ever, with a 16.3-inch touchscreen whose icons proved too small to press while driving

candidates.tagline: Pay $970 to monitor your brain. The sensor sits on the outside of your skull.
candidates.story: On November 6, 2026, Indian doctors — including AIIMS Delhi radiologists and hepatologist Dr Cyriac Abby Philips — declared that Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable (₹85,000 / ~$970), which claims to track cerebral blood flow in real time to slow aging, cannot do what it promises: a sensor on the outside of the skull can only measure blood flow to the face and scalp, not inside the brain.
candidates.why_funny: The founder of a food-delivery app spent $20 million of his own money building a brain blood-flow monitor, then doctors pointed out the sensor doesn't touch the brain, can't see the brain, and is separated from the brain by an entire skull.
candidates.alt: Deepinder Goyal, founder of the Temple brain-health startup, shown with the Temple wearable — a small sensor worn near the temple that claims to track cerebral blood flow through the skull in real time, whose science Indian doctors publicly challenged in November 2026
